title: Canadiens trade Brendan Gallagher to hometown Canucks: Source
content:
The Montreal Canadiens traded Brendan Gallagher to his hometown Vancouver Canucks on Monday, a league source, granted anonymity to speak about the trade that hasn’t been announced, told The Athletic.

The Canadiens were always going to do everything in their power to send Gallagher to his desired destination, and their willingness to retain 50 percent of his $6.5 million salary cap hit and $4 million actual salary is confirmation of the extent to which the Canadiens’ words were sincere.

Gallagher, who is expecting his second child with his wife Emma Fortin in July, said the top priority for him was to find a team near family, either his family in Vancouver or his wife’s family in Montreal.

“First and foremost, the priority is my family. So that’s No. 1 always. I’ve got a daughter that’s going to be under 2 and a newborn. She can’t be doing that alone,” Gallagher told The Athletic last week. “So we need to be in a position where we’re generally close (to family) and we can get some help. And then after that, I want to be in a position where you have purpose. You’re always trying to win, that’s always the goal. But that’s one thing I’ve kind of learned this year: when purpose is taken away from you, it affects me as a person. I think it would affect anyone in their job.”

But Vancouver was clearly Gallagher’s top desired destination, and the Canadiens did what was necessary to get him home by retaining the maximum amount of salary and getting nothing in return.

Gallagher, 34, grew up in nearby Tsawwassen, B.C., and played his junior hockey for the Vancouver Giants. He scored seven goals and 23 points in 77 games with the Canadiens this season, one year after putting up 21 goals and 38 points in 82 games. But his ice time dwindled as the season went on, and by March 14, in a home game against the San Jose Sharks, Gallagher was healthy scratched for the first time since the opening game of his rookie season in 2013. He was scratched for the final four games of the regular season and only played three of the 19 Canadiens playoff games this season.

The writing was on the wall for Gallagher long before that healthy scratch, but he appreciated the Canadiens’ transparency with him.

“I respect honesty,” he said, “and they’ve been honest.”

As difficult as it is for him to leave the only NHL franchise he has ever played for, he is excited for the opportunity to prove he can still contribute on the ice, and also go back to the net-crashing, possession-based identity that made Gallagher one of the league’s most analytically effective players for years.

“Marty (St. Louis) had a certain way of playing, and I had to adapt, and honestly, I feel like playing that way maybe extended my career a couple of years because it took less of a toll,” he said. “But there were certain areas of my game where, when I’m at my best, I’d also like to get back to that. I’d like to be a little bit more of a shot-volume guy and be around the net a little bit more.

“For me, my identity as a player, maybe I’ve taken a little bit of a step away from that, and I’d like to get back to that and see what happens.”

A young, rebuilding Canucks team will be eager to find out as well.

This story will be updated.
